summary: Iteration 12 hardening regression. All 6 requested items pass. Backend: 7/8 tests in /tmp/test_iter12.py pass against the public URL. The 1 failure is caused by the platform ingress, not the app (see CORS). The existing in-process suite passes 111/111. Frontend (Playwright): developer login works end to end. The flow is the QR/secret screen, a wrong code is rejected, 10 recovery codes appear, the done button is disabled until the checkbox is ticked, then the user lands on /sviluppatore. The login page shows only an 'Accedi' button, with no demo buttons or text. The invite page for an existing user with 2FA shows #pw and invite-totp-code (no confirm-password field). An empty code is blocked by the 'required' attribute, a wrong code shows 'Codice di verifica non valido o già usato.', and a valid code redirects to /login with invite-accepted-notice and the email prefilled. On the owner A Members page, owner B shows no 'Azzera verifica' and no 'Disattiva'. The collaborator shows both buttons, and reset-2fa-{id} gives the 'Verifica azzerata' toast. API: A -> B reset-2fa returns 403 and deactivate returns 403, and B's session still works. Existing-user invite: no code 401, wrong code 401, wrong password with a valid code 401, valid code 200 with no access_token, the token is then 404, and the memberships are added. Collaborator: deactivate gives 200 and the old session gets 401, then activate 200, then reset-2fa 200, and the next login returns setup_required. The developer password and the old demo password appear 0 times in the working tree (excluding node_modules/.git/test_reports/backend/.env), in the served JS bundle and in the backend logs. App-level CORS is correct: localhost:8001 with Origin evil.example returns no ACAO, and preflight returns 400. The preview origin is echoed exactly. NEW findings: an owner can still demote or revoke another owner's company access, an owner can deactivate the developer account, and the accept-invite endpoint has no lockout.

critical.issue: This bypasses the new 'a titolare cannot touch another titolare' rule. Owner A demoted owner B from titolare to commercialista on Co1 (200) and revoked B on Co2 (200), leaving B with 1 commercialista membership. The UI also still shows the role select and 'Revoca' on another owner's rows. Add the same target.is_owner -> 403 check to set_role and revoke (unless target == self), and hide or disable those controls in Members.js when m.is_owner.

deactivate has no is_developer check (reset_2fa has one). Owner A deactivated the developer account (200), which also bumps token_version and locks the developer out. It was re-activated by the same owner (200). activate also accepts any user id. Add 'if target.get("is_developer"): 404/403' to both. Consider also scoping to shared companies the way reset_2fa does.

minor.issue: Wrong password or wrong TOTP is not counted in failed_logins, and locked_until is not checked. 7 wrong attempts against an existing user returned 401 every time, with failed_logins=0 and no lockout. Someone holding an invite link has an unlimited password+TOTP guessing oracle. Reuse the login _fail/lockout logic.

A company created by owner A after owner B joined gives B no membership (B had 0 memberships on TEST_Co3). The owner-invite logic implies 'the group owner takes all companies'. Confirm whether new companies should auto-add every is_owner user.

Informational, not an app bug. A simple GET /api/health with Origin evil.example returns 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' through the preview ingress (Cloudflare/Google). The app itself (localhost:8001) returns no ACAO for evil.example, rejects the preflight with 400, and echoes only the configured preview origin. The ingress does not echo the evil origin itself. Note also that REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (gestione-tesoreria-...) differs from FRONTEND_URL/CORS_ORIGINS (7f4a3300-...). Make sure CORS_ORIGINS is set to the real production origin at deploy time.

ui_bugs.issue: For another titolare (m.is_owner), the role <select> and the 'Revoca' buttons are still shown and they work (see backend critical)

design_issues.screen: Login after accepting an invite as an existing 2FA user
issues: The invite-accepted-notice says 'Accedi con la password appena scelta: poi attiverai la verifica in due passaggi', which is wrong for an existing user who already has 2FA. Use different copy when the user existed.
invite-totp-code allows only 6 digits, so a user who lost their phone cannot use a recovery code here (the backend check_second_factor would accept one). Consider a recovery toggle like on Login.
The DEMO array ('titolare@demo.it') and the 'log del server' text are still in the served bundle (dead code, because SHOW_DEMO is false). Remove them to keep public code clean.

test_report_links: /tmp/test_iter12.py (outside /app as requested; reads DEV_PW, DEV_RC, BASE_URL and GOOD_ORIGIN from env)
action_items: Block set_role and revoke on another titolare (403), and hide the role select and Revoca for m.is_owner rows in Members.js
Add an is_developer guard (and ideally shared-company scoping) to /members/{id}/deactivate and /activate
Apply failed-login counting and lockout to the existing-user path of accept_invite

Optional: fix the invite-accepted notice copy for existing users; allow recovery codes on the invite page; remove the dead DEMO code from Login.js; decide whether new companies auto-include all group owners
critical_code_review_comments: members.deactivate checks is_owner but not is_developer; reset_2fa checks both. The checks are inconsistent
members.set_role and revoke only enforce 'at least one titolare' and do not protect other owners
accept_invite verifies the password and TOTP without calling _fail, so there is no lockout
